{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2017–18 |team=TCU Horned Frogs |image=TCU Horned Frogs logo.svg |conference=Big 12 Conference |short_conf=Big 12 |CoachRank= |APRank= |record=21–12 |conf_record=9–9 |head_coach=[[Jamie Dixon]] |hc_year=2nd |asst_coach1=David Patrick |asst_coach2=[[Ryan Miller (basketball coach)|Ryan Miller]] |ac2_year=2nd |asst_coach3=Corey Barker |stadium=[[Schollmaier Arena]] |champion=[[Emerald Coast Classic]] champions |bowl=[[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = First Round }} {{2017–18 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2017–18 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team''' represented [[Texas Christian University]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], led by head coach [[Jamie Dixon]] in his second season at TCU. The Horned Frogs competed as members of the [[Big 12 Conference]] and played their home games at [[Schollmaier Arena]] in [[Fort Worth, Texas]]. They finished the season 21–12, 9–9 in [[2017–18 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12 play]] to finish in fifth place. They lost in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] to [[2017–18 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], their first appearance in 20 years.{{cite news|last=Nguyen|first=Thuc Nhi|title=UCLA, Jamie Dixon reportedly in talks for men's basketball coaching job|date=April 3, 2019|work=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/04/03/ucla-jamie-dixon-reportedly-in-talks-for-mens-basketball-coaching-job/|accessdate=April 5, 2019}} Seeded No. 6 in the Midwest region, TCU lost in the first round to [[2017–18 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]]. ==Previous season== In 2016, the [[2016–17 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|Horned Frogs]] introduced Jamie Dixon, a former TCU letterman, as the new head men's basketball coach.{{cite web|title=Dixon Named Head Men's Basketball Coach|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032116aaa.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March 21, 2016|accessdate=November 9, 2017|archive-date=March 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322014246/http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032116aaa.html|url-status=dead}} In his first season after leaving [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pitt]] for his alma mater, Dixon led the Frogs to a 24–15, 6–12 [[2016–17 Big 12 Conference men's basketball season|Big 12]] record.{{cite web|title=Postgame Notes: TCU Wins NIT Championship|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/033017aaf.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March 30, 2017|accessdate=November 9, 2017}} The Frogs' 6–12 record and eighth-place finish was their best league mark since joining the Big 12 in 2012.{{cite web|title=TCU Opens Big 12 Championship with OU|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030617aac.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March 6, 2017|accessdate=November 9, 2017}} In the postseason, TCU defeated [[2016–17 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]]{{cite web|title=TCU routs Oklahoma, 82-63|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030817aaa.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March 8, 2017|accessdate=November 9, 2017}} and No. 1 [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]{{cite web|title=TCU stuns No. 1 Kansas 85-82 in Big 12 quarterfinals|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030917aaa.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March 9, basketball team|Iowa State]].{{cite web|title=TCU Falls to Iowa State in Big 12 Semifinals, 84-63|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031017aaa.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=March bball = yes }} ===Exhibition games in Australia=== The Frogs traveled to Sydney and Melbourne, Australia, from August 5–16, 2017, and played five exhibition games under International Basketball Federation (FIBA) rules.{{cite web|title=TCU Men to Play Five Games Down Under|url=http://www.gofrogs.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/080317aab.html|publisher=TCU Athletics|date=August 3, 2017|accessdate=August 13, 2017}} TCU's starting sophomore guard Jaylen Fisher missed the trip due to a knee injury, and incoming freshmen [[Lat Mayen]], an Australia native, and Kevin Samuel were unable to travel pending NCAA eligibility clearance. All three players were expected to be healthy and cleared prior to the season opener on November 10; however, the Frogs ultimately elected to redshirt Mayen and Samuel.{{cite web|title=TCU guard Fisher suffers knee injury, will miss Australia trip to have surgery|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article165687032.html|publisher=Fort Worth preseason coaches' poll, the highest-ever projection for the Frogs since joining the league in 2012 and being picked to finish ninth or tenth in each of their first five seasons.{{cite web|title=TCU
